newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says 1,300 Timor cars sold in March.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says 1,300 Timor cars sold in March.

text.p: Indonesian car distributor PT Timor Distributor Nasional (TDN), controlled by President Suharto's son, said on Monday that March sales of the national car Timor rose to 1,300 units but it was still below expectations.
"We sold some 1,300 (sedans) in March, up from around 900 in February," company president director Soemitro Soerachmad told a news conference.
TDN distributes the Timor sedan produced jointly by PT Timor Putra Nasional, controlled by the president's son Hutomo Mandala Putra, and KIA Motors of South Korea.
The Indonesian government last year awarded tax and tariff breaks to Timor Putra to produce the 1,600cc national car.
Japan, the United States and the European Union have complained to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) against the move, which they have labelled as an unfair trade practice.

Sales in March were not very encouraging and were likely to remain weak in April and May due to several public holidays during the period, Soerachmad said. He added that sales were expected to pick up in June.
Timor has forecast sales of some 40,000 units this year, or about 3,300 cars each month. The firm has so far sold about 12,000 cars since October last year.
Indonesia's total vehicle sales in 1996 were 331,150 units compared with 385,070 units in 1995.
